This conversation uses two-stage tool calling. First, call exactly the meta-tool below; do not call a real tool before the tool response arrives. Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

Meta-tool schema:
{
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "select_tool",
    "description": "Choose the one real tool that should handle the query.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "tool_name": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "tool_o",
            "tool_b",
            "tool_t",
            "tool_m",
            "tool_d",
            "tool_q",
            "tool_f",
            "tool_k",
            "tool_s",
            "tool_r",
            "tool_n",
            "tool_p",
            "tool_g",
            "tool_l",
            "tool_c",
            "tool_h",
            "tool_a",
            "tool_j",
            "tool_e",
            "tool_i"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "tool_name"
      ],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  }
}

I've been hearing my grandson talk about something called 'cryptocurrencies' while he's been visiting. Now, I don't pretend to understand all that digital money business, but I figure I should at least know what the fuss is about. Could you start by giving me the latest general news and updates on the whole crypto market? If there's any significant news about a specific cryptocurrency, like Bitcoin or Ethereum—those names I've heard mentioned—then maybe dig into that one a bit deeper. I'd like to know what's making waves out there, even if I'm still partial to good old cash in my wallet.

description.description: Optional description of changes made in this version. Defaults to empty string if not provided.

auto_publish.description: When true, automatically publishes the new version for stakeholders. Default is false.

numero_dias.description: Number of recent days to return records for. Must be a numeric string. Default: '30' if not specified

I found a beautiful highlight reel from the Newark Arts Collective that showcases their previous events, but I'm struggling to download it for editing. The link is [https://www.instagram.com/stories/highlights/17841467954261933/](https://www.instagram.com/stories/highlights/17841467954261933/). Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

I need to analyze the latest Instagram story from a logistics industry influencer, then download a related post mentioned in their story. Here's the influencer's story URL: [https://www.instagram.com/stories/logistics_trends/12345] First, download their story to review the content. Based on what's in that story, they often reference specific posts in their highlights - I'll need you to identify the highlighted post they're promoting (you'll see it in the story's metadata or media) and download that post next. Let me know when you've completed both steps.

Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

I'm creating a networking event campaign and need to generate personalized placeholder headshots for 30 attendees based on their actual professional backgrounds. I have a list of attendees' names and current companies. Can you help me search for their LinkedIn profiles to understand their roles and industries, then create realistic AI-generated headshots that reflect each person's professional context? For example, I'd start with "Sarah Chen" who works at "NVIDIA" - can you find her LinkedIn info and generate a professional headshot that incorporates elements relevant to her tech/AI background?
